1  ...RESPONDENTS  (BY SRI THEJESH P., HCGP FOR R1)
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:40728
CRL.P No. 11126 of 2022

THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.482 OF THE CR.P.C PRAYING TO QUASH THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS PENDING AGAINST THE PETITIONER AND OTHER 8 ACCUSED IN C.C.NO.1120/2016 (CR.NO.124/2015) ON THE FILE OF IV ADDL.C.M.M., BENGALURU WHICH HAS BEEN REGISTERED ON THE BASIS OF THE CHARGE SHEET FILED BY 1ST RESPONDENT i.e., RAJAJINAGAR POLICE STATION, FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 323, 498A, 419, 506 OF IPC AND SECTION 3 AND 4 OF DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT ARRAYING THE PETITIONER AS ACCUSED NO.1.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.1120/2016 (arising out of Crime No.124/2015), registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 419 and 506 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Learned counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 would in unison submit that during the pendency of this petition, the parties to the lis have arrived at a settlement and are living together happily.
A joint affidavit of the parties is filed before this Court seeking to quash the proceedings.

The relevant paragraphs of the joint affidavit read as follows:
"JOINT AFFIDAVIT FILED BY THE PETITIONER AND RESPONDENT NO.2.
xxxx 2.
Amicable Resolution:
With the intervention of our elders, well-wishers and friends, we have amicably settled all our matrimonial disputes and misunderstandings.
We have reconciled and Mr. Mohan Panchariya vs State Of Karnataka on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159087185/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 are now living together peacefully and happily as husband and wife along with our minor daughter.

3. No Objection to Quashing of the Case:
Respondent No.2 (wife) has no objection to the quashing of the criminal case in C.C.No.1120/2016 filed against Petitioner No.1 and his family members.
We both request the Hon'ble Court to kindly quash the said criminal proceedings, as continuing the case would serve no useful purpose.
4. Voluntary Compromise:
We further declare that the compromise has been made voluntarily, without any force, coercion, or undue influence from any party.
Both of us are fully aware of the contents of this affidavit and the legal implications of the quashing of the criminal case.

5. Personal Appearance:
We are willing to appear before this Hon'ble Court as and when directed, to confirm the NC: 2024:KHC:40728 settlement and our no objection to quashing the proceedings."

In the light of the afore-quoted joint affidavit, though few of the offences are non-compoundable, as it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to terminate the proceedings against the petitioner, as the same is not against the State.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1120/2016 pending before the IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru stand quashed.
